svg.title: Environment: values passed to child programs.
svg.desc: A shell variable holds a named value. Assignment stores it without spaces around the equals sign; quoted expansion inserts its value as one argument. In Bash, an ordinary unexported variable stays in the current shell. Starting with DEMO_MESSAGE unset, assigning Hello and starting a child Bash with printf produces empty angle brackets. After export DEMO_MESSAGE, the child prints Hello inside angle brackets. Outer single quotes pass unchanged code to the child, which expands its own variable. A downward diagram shows inheritance, not changes to parents or existing programs. Export is neither global nor permanent.
svg.text: The environment holds named values for child programs: programs this shell starts.
A shell variable holds a named value. Assignment stores it; no spaces around =.
DEMO_MESSAGE=Hello stores Hello; "$DEMO_MESSAGE" inserts it as one value.
Requires Bash; DEMO_MESSAGE starts unset (not assigned). bash -c starts a child shell.
Output: <> — without export, this variable stays in the current shell.
Output: <Hello> — export passes the value to newly started children.
Outer single quotes pass unchanged code; the child expands "$DEMO_MESSAGE".
Not global or permanent: no change to parent shells or already-running programs.
